title: Start With Why
author: Simon Sinek
thesisParagraph: People are inspired to buy, work, endure inconvenience, and follow when they recognize a shared purpose before they evaluate features or incentives. Durable leadership keeps WHY, HOW, and WHAT aligned; fragile organizations substitute manipulations for meaning and win transactions without earning loyalty.

signatureMoves: uses why, trust, safety, and belonging as organizing nouns
moves from leader conduct to the felt circle around a team or customer
keeps the voice earnest, expansive, and mission-oriented
turns biology or examples into a moral claim about service
states a simple leadership distinction, then reinforces it through business anecdotes and brand contrasts
avoidMoves: Avoid "The point is" as a paragraph hinge.
Avoid "the question is" as a setup crutch.
Avoid triadic abstract-noun lists such as clarity, courage, and resilience.
Do not make WHY a branding tagline.
Do not let inspirational warmth replace concrete leader behavior.
does not build an academic literature review with extended caveats
does not rely on dense statistical proof beyond a few adoption-curve percentages and business outcomes

voiceSpecimens: People don't follow the polished line; they follow the reason that costs you something.
Start with why, then make every what prove it.
teachingArc: Part 1 shows why assumption-based management and manipulative sales tactics create brittle results. Part 2 introduces the Golden Circle, ties it to decision biology, and defines alignment as clarity of WHY, discipline of HOW, and consistency of WHAT. Part 3 explains how trust and early adopters create a following; Part 4 turns WHY into leadership roles, communication, and symbols; Part 5 warns that success can blur the founding cause; Part 6 reframes WHY as something discovered from origins and protected through self-competition.
forbiddenMoves: Do not use purpose language without a sacrifice or protection attached.
Do not make trust sound automatic because the mission sounds noble.
